name: MicroFreak
popularity: Long-running budget hybrid synth (2019 onward, still current with firmware 5) with wide press coverage, e.g. Sound On Sound review (https://www.soundonsound.com/reviews/arturia-microfreak); no sales-chart figure was checked.

bendRangeSemitones.how: Per preset: Utility > Preset > Bend Range, 0 to 24 semitones (manual v5.0.1 p.26). Factory default value not stated in the manual. No CC for it.

respondsToNotes.cc7Volume: CC 7 is not in the manual's CC table (Appendix D). Treat as not received.
respondsToNotes.cc1ModWheel: CC 1 is not in the manual's CC table. The MicroFreak has no mod wheel.
respondsToNotes.programChange: The manual does not mention receiving Program Change. Unknown.
respondsToNotes.velocity: Utility > Preset > Velo Amp Mod (0-10) sets how velocity affects volume; Press Mode selects Aftertouch or Velocity for the keyboard. Velocity response to incoming MIDI notes is implied, not explicitly stated.
respondsToNotes.cc64Sustain: CC 64 is listed as 'Keyboard Hold (toggle)', i.e. it toggles the Hold button, not a classic momentary sustain. Treat with care: each value change may flip Hold on/off.

controls.label: TYPE
controls.notes: Selects oscillator engine. Value-to-type table is not in the manual. Arturia forum report (forum.arturia.com/t/6268) says transmitted and received CC 9 values do not match for about 11 types, so do not derive receive ranges from what the synth sends. Leave steps unset until measured.

controls.label: CUTOFF
controls.notes: Manual p.122: CC 23 value 0 closes the filter fully, 127 opens it fully.

controls.label: RISE
controls.notes: Appendix D says 102. The tutorial on p.123 says the Rise knob sent CC 5, which conflicts with Glide = 5 in Appendix D; Appendix D is used here.

controls.label: AMOUNT

controls.label: ATTACK
controls.notes: The main envelope drives the filter by default; it also drives the amp only when the Amp Mod switch is on. Role set to filter_attack for that reason.

controls.label: DECAY/RELEASE
controls.notes: Single Decay/Release stage. Appendix D name: 'Envelope Decay'. Same Amp Mod caveat as Attack.

controls.label: SUSTAIN
controls.notes: Same Amp Mod caveat as Attack.

controls.label: FILTER AMT
controls.notes: Appendix D name: 'Filter Amount'. Panel label taken from manual text ('Filter Amt').

controls.label: RATE
controls.notes: Free (unsynced) rate. Used when LFO Sync is off.

controls.label: RATE (synced)
controls.notes: Synced rate (time divisions). Used when LFO Sync is on. Same physical knob as CC 93.

controls.label: RATE
controls.notes: Arp/Seq free tempo.

controls.label: RATE (synced)
controls.notes: Arp/Seq synced rate. Same physical knob as CC 91.

controls.label: SPICE
controls.notes: Spice amount set via the touch strip, not a knob. Only audible when Arp or Seq runs.

controls.label: HOLD
controls.notes: Appendix D: 'Keyboard Hold (toggle)'.

setup: Set the receive channel: press Utility, go to MIDI > Input chan, choose All or the channel your app sends on (manual p.120 and p.96).
If notes play but no sound changes come back to the app, that is the transmit side: Utility > MIDI > Knob send CCs = On (only needed for the synth to send, not to receive).
If the keyboard seems dead, check Utility > MIDI > Local is On (Local Off disconnects the keyboard from the engine; external MIDI still plays).
After loading a preset, physical knob positions do not match the sound. CC messages set the value directly regardless of knob position.

sources.what: MicroFreak User Manual v5.0.1 (EN), Appendix D 'CC# Values' p.141-142 (PDF p.146-147); MIDI chapter p.120-123; Utility tables p.26, p.96
Arturia forum thread: CC 9 oscillator type send vs receive value mismatch (user report, Arturia staff acknowledged)

confidence: high for the 20 CC numbers (manufacturer table, firmware 5 manual); low for CC 9 value ranges and the default receive channel, which the manual does not state.

name: MiniFreak
popularity: Arturia's 6-voice polyphonic follow-up to the MicroFreak (2022), widely reviewed; no sales-chart figure was checked.

bendRangeSemitones.how: Sound Edit > Keyboard > Bend Range, 1 to 12 semitones (manual v4.0.1 p.90). Default not stated. No CC for it.

respondsToNotes.cc7Volume: CC 7 is not in the manual's MIDI implementation chart. Oscillator volumes are CC 17 and 21. Treat master volume as not controllable by CC.
respondsToNotes.programChange: 512 presets = 4 banks of 128. Send Bank Select then Program Change (manual p.115). Utility > MIDI > Program Change must be on to send and receive.
respondsToNotes.velocity: Keyboard and engine use velocity; engine also accepts polyphonic aftertouch from external MIDI (manual p.86).

setup: Open Utility: hold Shift and press Sound Edit/Utility (button lights pale blue).
Turn the Preset/Edit encoder to MIDI, click it.
Set Input Channel to All or the channel your app sends on, click to save.
Set MIDI From to USB (or the port you use).
Check Local Control is On and MIDI Seq/Synth is 'MIDI > Synth' (default) so incoming notes go straight to the synth.
Incoming CC is always accepted, except while MiniFreak V software is connected and talking to the synth (manual p.117). Close MiniFreak V first.

sources.what: MiniFreak User Manual v4.0.1 (EN), section 16.2.5 MIDI implementation chart p.116-117 (PDF p.121-122); Utility > MIDI p.108; Bend Range p.90

confidence: high for CC numbers (manufacturer chart in the current hardware manual; firmware is now 5.0.1 and the v5 hardware manual was not published separately, so a firmware-5 CC change is possible but none was found); panel labels for shared knobs are annotated with the slot in brackets.

name: Bass Station II
popularity: Novation's long-selling analogue mono synth (2013 onward, still sold with firmware updates such as AFX mode); no sales-chart figure was checked.

bendRangeSemitones.how: Hold Function and press upper C# (Oscillator: Pitch Bend Range), -24 to +24 (p.61). Init patch value is 12 (p.70). Also CC 107 'Bend Amount' per the MIDI chart.

respondsToNotes.cc1ModWheel: The v5 chart prints 'mod cc 0', almost certainly a typo for CC 1 but not confirmed in a manufacturer document. Leave unverified.
respondsToNotes.programChange: Chart lists patch inc/dec via program change 0-127.
respondsToNotes.velocity: Velocity response depends on the patch: Velocity: Amp Env (CC 112) defaults to 0 = no velocity effect.

setup: Set the MIDI channel: hold Function/Exit, press upper G# key, release, use Patch/Value buttons to pick the channel (default 1, saved on power-down).
Leave Local On (upper A) unless you want the keyboard disconnected; Local Off is not needed for receiving MIDI.
To send an NRPN: CC 99 = NRPN MSB, CC 98 = NRPN LSB, CC 6 = value. Pitch bend and aftertouch are standard messages.

sources.what: Bass Station II User Guide v5 (EN), 'MIDI parameters list' p.71-74; On-key functions p.61-64; hardware overview p.8-12; init values p.69-70

confidence: high for CC and NRPN numbers (manufacturer chart, current v5 guide); medium for switch value-to-position mappings, which the chart mostly omits, and for the two chart typos noted (mod 'cc 0', noise '23.55').
